title: Mechanistic comparison of DEHP and substitutes ATBC/ATEC in spermatogenic failure: integrated GEO data analysis, network toxicology, and experimental validation
content:
Abstract
While di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a known reproductive toxicant, the safety of its substitutes acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) and acetyl triethyl citrate (ATEC) remains unclear. This study compared their molecular mechanisms in spermatogenic failure using an integrated approach. Potential targets of DEHP, ATBC, and ATEC were predicted and cross-referenced with spermatogenic failure-related genes from disease databases. Protein–protein interaction networks, enrichment analyses, and GEO data analysis were performed to identify key targets and pathways. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations assessed binding interactions. Experimentally, TM4 Sertoli cells were treated with the plasticizers, and effects on viability (CCK-8) and expression of CDK4, PIK3CA, TLR4, and downstream phospho-proteins (Rb, Akt, p65) were examined. Enrichment analysis linked shared targets to cell cycle, apoptosis, PI3K-Akt signaling, and inflammation. Cross-referencing with GEO datasets identified CDK4 as a key target for DEHP and PIK3CA for ATBC; ATEC targeted PIK3CA, TLR4, and CDK4. DEHP showed the strongest binding to CDK4 (−7.579 kcal/mol). In TM4 cells, 200 μM of each compound reduced viability, while 100 μM downregulated CDK4, PIK3CA, and TLR4 expression and decreased p-Rb, p-Akt, and p-p65 levels. DEHP bound strongly to CDK4, hinting at direct cell cycle disruption and spermatogenic failure, whereas ATBC and ATEC showed broader, weaker binding, suggesting indirect mechanisms.
